newsitem.title: FRANCE: France to let thousands of illegal immigrants stay.
newsitem.headline: France to let thousands of illegal immigrants stay.

text.p: Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin was to announce on Tuesday that France's new left-wing government would give residence permits to tens of thousands of illegal immigrants, government sources said.

They said Jospin was to announce the measure at a meeting later in the day with a group of Africans who had marched from the southwestern city of Angouleme to request residence papers that the previous right-wing government had refused them.
The sources said that orders would be given to central government representatives across France to grant the documents to immigrants fulfilling certain criteria.

The move, which would affect between 20,000 and 40,000 people, is an interim measure until Jospin can fulfil election campaign pledges to repeal hardline immigration laws pushed through by former Gaullist interior ministers Jean-Louis Debre and Charles Pasqua.

Those who would qualify include parents of children born in France, spouses of immigrants with legal status, those who would be in danger if sent home, foreigners receiving extensive medical care, students, and foreigners "well-integrated in French society".

Jospin vowed before the left took power in June 1 parliamentary elections to abolish the hardline laws, but the step looks certain to raise an outcry on the right. Opinion polls show a majority of French people want the legislation to stay.
The immigrant issue sparked nationwide controversy last August when police stormed a church and forcibly evacuated some 200 Africans who had taken refuge there to avoid expulsion.
Magistrates later overturned orders expelling most of them, but they were not given residence documents, leaving most of them with an unclear legal status.
The protesters, called the "sans-papiers" (those without papers), say they once enjoyed residence rights but were deprived of them when the immigration laws were toughened.
There are an estimated five million foreigners in France, of whom about one million, mostly North Africans, are thought to be illegal.
